title: Mental adding and subtracting with jumps
summary: Show each addition and subtraction as jumps on a number line: tens then ones, or to the next ten first.
guide: On a {{term:number-line}}, {{term:addition}} is a jump to the right and {{term:subtraction}} is a jump to the left.
The arcs show the jumps. You tap where each jump lands; the number on the arc says how far you jumped, and the number under the point says where you landed.
For two-digit numbers, split the second number: for 37 + 25, jump 20 (to 57) and then 5 (to 62). Sometimes it's easier to jump to the next ten first: for 8 + 5, jump 2 to 10, then 3 more.
In class you may draw an empty number line with just the numbers you need. This one has marks so you can check each jump.
You can drag a point, or tap it and move it with the arrow keys. "Clear points" starts again.

engine.label-line: Number line: tap to place a point

three-and-five.title: 3 + 5 on the line
three-and-five.prompt: First jump 3 from 0, then 5 more. Tap where each jump lands. What is 3 + 5?
three-and-five.hint: The first jump lands on 3. From 3, count on 5 more: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.
three-and-five.why: If you jump 5 first and then 3, where do you land? Why?
three-and-five.model: On 8 again. Both ways you go 8 along altogether; only the order of the jumps has changed. 5 + 3 = 8

feedback.count: Make two jumps: one for 3 and one for 5 more.
feedback.wrong: Look at the numbers on the arcs: one should be +3 and the other +5. Start counting from the next mark, not the one you're on.

next-ten.title: Jump to 10 first
next-ten.prompt: What is 8 + 5? Start at 8. Jump to 10 first, then the rest.
next-ten.hint: From 8 to 10 is 2. That leaves 3 of the 5.
next-ten.why: Why does jumping to 10 first make it easier?
next-ten.model: Adding to 10 is easy: 10 + 3 = 13. You only need to know what makes 8 up to 10 (2) and what is left of the 5 (3).

feedback.count: Make two jumps: one to 10 and one for the rest.
feedback.wrong: The first jump should land on 10. The arcs, +2 and +3, should add up to 5.

tens-then-ones.title: 37 + 25: tens first
tens-then-ones.prompt: Start at 37. Jump 20 first, then 5. Predict first: is the answer more or less than 60?
tens-then-ones.hint: 37 + 20: only the tens digit changes. Then jump 5 more.
tens-then-ones.why: Why is 37 + 20 easy to work out?
tens-then-ones.model: 20 is two tens. Each jump of 10 adds one to the tens digit: 47, 57. The ones digit, 7, doesn't change.

feedback.wrong: Look at the arcs: the first should say +20 and the second +5. Read the number under each point too.

back-tens-then-ones.title: 62 − 27: jumping back
back-tens-then-ones.prompt: Now subtract: start at 62. Jump 20 to the left first, then 7.
back-tens-then-ones.hint: 62 − 20 = 42. From 42, jump back 7: you'll go past 40.
back-tens-then-ones.why: Maryam said 62 − 27 = 45, because 7 − 2 = 5. What went wrong?
back-tens-then-ones.model: She took 2 away from 7, but it should be 7 taken away from 2 (from 42). On the line, from 42 we jump back 7: 2 to get to 40, then 5 more to 35.

feedback.count: Make two jumps back: −20 first, then −7.
feedback.wrong: Subtracting means jumping left. The arcs should say −20 and −7. It isn't 45: jump back 7 from 42.

three-digit.prompt: This line goes up in tens. Start at 530: jump back 200 first, then 80.
three-digit.hint: 530 − 200 = 330. From 330, jump back 80: 30 to get to 300, then 50 more.
three-digit.why: Reza did it like this: 530 − 300 = 230, then forward 20. Why forward 20?
three-digit.model: 300 is 20 more than 280. Jumping back 300 goes 20 too far, so we jump forward 20: 230 + 20 = 250

feedback.count: Make two jumps back: −200 first, then −80.
feedback.wrong: The arcs should say −200 and −80. Each small mark is 10; read the number under the point.
